sections.title: Identification and habitat
sections.text: Anthriscus sylvestris (cow parsley) is a biennial or perennial of the carrot family, native across temperate Eurasia and also present in montane tropical Africa. It commonly grows in hedges, woodland edges and grassland. Finely divided leaves and white umbels are not enough to distinguish it safely from poisonous umbellifers.

sections.title: Size and flowers
sections.text: Flowering stems commonly reach about 60–150 cm; compound umbels are several centimetres across, with dimensions varying by habitat. The plate's airy white umbels and divided leaves fit the species.

sections.title: Food and safety
sections.text: Some regional references report young leaves as edible, but cow parsley can be confused with highly poisonous Conium maculatum (poison hemlock) and other Apiaceae. Do not identify or eat it from this plate or a short description; no Conium image is included here.
